slides.headline: It looks like a love scene. Look again.
slides.sub: William Holman Hunt, The Awakening Conscience, 1853

slides.headline: London, 1853
slides.text: A London room, 1853. A young man has pulled a woman onto his lap at the piano. A happy couple? Not quite.

slides.headline: Him
slides.text: He is still singing, carefree, one arm around her. He has no idea that something has just changed in her.

slides.headline: Her
slides.text: She suddenly rises from his lap, staring at something beyond the room. Her face shows a painful realisation.

slides.headline: The hand
slides.text: Look at her hands. Rings on almost every finger, but none on the wedding finger. She is not his wife but his mistress.

slides.headline: The cat
slides.text: Under the table, a cat plays with a bird it has caught. The bird is trying to escape. Just like her.

slides.headline: The clues
slides.text: A glove tossed aside, tangled threads, a song sheet called Tears, Idle Tears. Everything in this room hints at a wasted life.

slides.headline: The mirror
slides.text: Now the mirror behind them. It reflects a sunlit spring garden, the world outside. That is what she sees: a way out.

slides.headline: Too painful
slides.text: The buyer found her face too painful to live with and asked Hunt to soften it. Hunt repainted it. Does she leave him?
